checks.question: Are ownership, exports and dependency direction portable and one-way?
checks.detail: network-routing has no runtime/internal dependencies; account-pool declares only network-routing via workspace:*. Source imports stay local and public exports expose the portable contracts. Repository boundary checker passed.

checks.question: Are entry points lightweight and clock/transport capabilities injected?
checks.detail: ES2023-only package compilation passed. Source contains no DOM/Node/GM/Vue/music-model imports, wall-clock access, concrete HTTP, persistence or raw credentials. Runtime supplies monotonic clock/timers and execute callbacks. configurationKey is an opaque reference.

checks.question: Do races, deadlines and cancellation stop all future work and release resources?
checks.detail: Existing serial/parallel/deadline/write-safety tests pass. Synchronous cancellation inside isAvailable still starts one transport and leaves one timer; reentrant cancellation from an abort subscriber still allows onFailure to run. Both failures share missing terminal-state rechecks after user callbacks.

checks.question: Are proxy health, explicit direct permission and non-replayable operations isolated from runtime authority?
checks.detail: Proven proxy failures alone reach backoff with a correct classifier; unknown platform errors/timeouts stay neutral. Explicit proxy support and direct permission are checked, unsafe writes are not replayed, stale generations cannot affect health, and proxy disable/reconfiguration cancels old leases. Renaming preserves leases. No GM/Rust behavior was accepted. RoutingError remains a portable exception and runtime AppErrorState conversion is deferred to B12.

checks.question: Do owner tests cover the lifecycle contract sufficiently?
checks.detail: All 24 retained tests pass with a deterministic injected clock. Six temporary lifecycle probes produce four passes and two reproducible failures. The two callback-reentrancy branches lack permanent regression coverage; repair must add owner tests. Temporary probes were removed after archiving, so product implementation and retained tests remain unchanged.

findings.title: Reentrant cancellation from injected callbacks does not stop subsequent executor work.
findings.trigger: isAvailable synchronously cancels the operation and returns true. A related branch occurs when fail() cancels an attempt and its abort listener synchronously cancels the parent.
findings.observed: The first probe receives RoutingError(cancelled) but execute still runs once and the manual clock retains one timer. The second receives RoutingError(cancelled) but onFailure still runs once.
findings.effect: A caller may start transport after receiving terminal cancellation and retain its timer; callback side effects may run after cancellation. The newly created attempt misses finish() cleanup because finish already marked the operation done. Late success remains suppressed, so this is a cancellation/resource defect rather than a demonstrated stale-result publication.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Recheck terminal state immediately after reentrant availability and cancellation callbacks, before creating/scheduling/starting more work or invoking failure classification. Add permanent regression tests for both branches under network-routing/test/attempts.test.ts, then rerun routing and direct account-pool consumer tests/typechecks.
findings.limits: Reproduced through the public shared executor with legal synchronous callbacks. The one-hop account consumer currently uses a simple synchronous catalog availability check; no production GM/Rust manifestation or introduction by the latest refactor was established. Severity is limited to the demonstrated shared cancellation contract.
